title: Controlled microphase separation and strain programming in hydrogel fibers toward biomimetic architectures and properties
core_idea: Fabricate sodium polyacrylate–polyacrylamide composite hydrogel fibers by wet-spinning where antisolvent-induced microphase separation generates hydrogen-bonded nanoclusters, and subsequent post-drawing strain programming promotes uniaxial polymer alignment and controlled crystallization to replicate the hierarchical architecture of natural spider silk.
tldr: A wet-spinning and strain-programming strategy controls microphase separation and polymer alignment in pana–pam hydrogel fibers to mimic spider-silk hierarchical structure for biomimetic, multifunctional fibers.
